title: Grateful Dead Live at Kiel Auditorium on 1973-10-30
source: MSR > D > PCM > D > CD patched with AUD

ai_review.summary: A soundboard capture of a late‑October ’73 show with crisp audio (despite some noise‑reduction processing) and a stellar second set highlighted by a rare Dark Star → Stella Blue → Eyes sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording is a solid soundboard source; most listeners praise its clarity while noting that a modest noise‑reduction pass was applied, leaving the mix generally clean but not pristine. Musically the concert shines in the second set – a cosmic Dark Star, a flowing Stella Blue into an incendiary Eyes, and a soaring Weather Report Suite make this one of the era’s top performances, though a few feel the first set is comparatively mellow. Overall the show is celebrated for its inspired jams and tight playing.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews (12 × 5‑star, several praising specific jams) highlight an excellent performance, while the recording is described as decent to good with only minor technical caveats.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear overall mix; a noise‑reduction process was applied (noted by a reviewer) but retains instrument separation. One comment mentions the sound could be better, yet no major dropouts or distortion are reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is solid but considered less exciting than typical ’73 shows; the second set delivers a rare Dark Star → Stella Blue → Eyes progression, a flowing Weather Report Suite and a standout MLB jam, giving the concert an uplifting, space‑y feel despite some listeners finding it a bit mellow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals described as gorgeous with a slightly megaphone‑like texture; guitar work noted as cosmic and tightly intertwined with Phil’s bass during Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass ‘booms’ and resonates, delivering powerful “bombs” on Dark Star; praised for tight, inspired interplay with Jerry.
band_member_comments.Bob: Shines on the pre‑verse Dark Star jam and the energetic Eyes outro; his rhythm guitar presence is highlighted as essential to the sound.
